strings.en:
My dearest Winter Sky,  
  
Not a day has passed since I saw you last when I have not thought of you. On cold, clear nights, I stare up at the sky and wonder where you are. And when the flowers are in bloom, I think of the days of our hunt, following tracks through the blossoming arrowleaf.  
  
Life here continues as always. I am still making medicine for the village and helping my mother keep things in order. We have not seen another famine in a long while now. I am often lonely here, but I am well.  
  
I hope that you are eating enough and staying warm and that you always find your prey. I hope that the cold winds cannot find you and that your head finds easy rest each night. And I hope that you will stay well until the day I find you again.  
  
Forever yours,
Flowering Meadow

Skup is gone. They're all gone. I've put myself in harm's way looking for signs of them, to no avail.  
  
After an extended search, I returned to my prior observation point among the waterfalls. I watched as more of the creatures were gathered and escorted through the door of the towerlike rock structure, but at that distance I could not make out individual faces. I don't know that I could recognize their faces regardless, as it was their voices that distinguished them for me. Perhaps I watched as my new friends were carted away to...Alchemy knows what.  
  
Ah, Skup. I hope this was all jumping at shadows. That you and Grink and Bosh and Till are being fed and housed and—  
  
I'm lying to myself. I know I'm lying to myself. I have to. The reality of this situation is too cruel to consider. I have to. I have to, so I can continue with my duty—even if it is imagined duty.  
  
Northward.  
  
—Operative Selly

Chapter 1—The Shore  
  
Cliff found himself standing along a lonely shore, on a lonely beach, on a lonely island. Oh, how lonely was Cliff here on this beach all by himself. While Cliff had a home not too far away in a bustling village with a lovely family, he would find himself along this shore almost every night staring at a rock far out in the water.  
  
Oh, how lonely that rock must be, alone in the ocean, thought Cliff. Cliff knew not how to swim or row a boat.  
  
"Woe is me!" ~~Hank~~ Cliff would holler out into the sea. "I am so alone on this beach, and that rock is so alone in the sea. If only I knew how to visit the lonely rock!"  
  
But there was nothing Cliff could do. So he gave up and went home.  
  
The End

Day 1  
  
Aye, maybe we're as doomed as they all say, but we'll not just accept our fates here. Thing is, cobbling together something that'll float ain't an issue—entire shore's littered with shipwrecks, after all. Got an infinite supply of parts! Just don't have an infinite supply of lives...  
  
Day 23  
  
Fair winds today, finally. Rocc managed to get the ship—though might be optimistic calling it a ship, more a raft with a sail if you ask me—out into the bay farther than I could spot him without a spyglass. Thought maybe he was gone forever 'til he showed up at the pub, clothes soaked and in tatters. Said he hit a patch of foul weather just beyond sight of shore, then he had to outrace a shark back to the beach.  
  
Day 51  
  
Few more test runs up and down the coast, all successful. It's when we head east a certain ways, something always happens—swarming crabs, foul weather, thick fog, you name it. But this ship is solid. It's now or never. Rocc and I are going for it. Our lives are back on the mainland, not in this tiny patch of sand. We're going home to our families, or we'll die trying.  
  
Day 52  
  
Rocc here. Don't know what to write. Paldius was the writing type, not me. He didn't make it. Fog was thick as stew. Crabs swarmed us. Couldn't see my own hands in front of my face. When we came back out of the fog—facing west, somehow—Pal was gone. I limped what was left of the ship home.  
  
I'm done. Can't do this anymore. Writing or sailing. Time to admit we're stuck. I'm stuck.  
  
Good-bye, friend.
